title: canopy-task-completion-signal-v1
description: Canopy emits an explicit completion signal when an agent closes a task via `canopy_task_complete`. The `should_continue` flag is the agent's stated intent about whether follow-on dispatch should proceed; `status` reports the agent's assessment of the outcome, and `next_action` optionally tells the orchestrator what to dispatch next. `status` here is the signal's reported outcome and is distinct from the stored canopy TaskStatus, which this signal does not change. Producer: canopy/src/tools/task.rs (tool_task_complete). Consumer: hymenium (dispatch loop — reads should_continue and next_action to decide whether and how to continue the workflow). This signal rides alongside the existing task-detail response and does not change TaskStatus or the stored Task shape.

task_id.description: Identifier of the task that was completed.

agent_id.description: Identifier of the agent that emitted the completion signal. Mirrors the agent_id passed to tool_task_complete; lets the orchestrator decide the next assignee.

status.description: Agent's reported outcome. `completed` closed normally; `failed` could not finish and is handing back; `blocked` is stalled on an external dependency; `needs_review` is finished pending verification. This is the signal's assessment, not the stored canopy TaskStatus.

should_continue.description: Agent's explicit intent: true asks the orchestrator to continue dispatching follow-on work, false signals a clean stop. Optional; an absent value is treated as false (stop).

next_action.description: Optional hint describing the follow-on work when should_continue is true. Absent or null means the orchestrator decides. Ignored when should_continue is false.

follow_up_task_id.description: Existing task the orchestrator should dispatch next, if the agent named one.

directive.description: Free-text continuation instruction for the orchestrator.

summary.description: Closure summary recorded by the agent. Mirrors the completion_summary evidence stored on the task.
